Home
‘Growing together in wisdom and love; discovering life in all its fullness.’
Welcome to the website of Malmesbury C of E Primary School. We are a school of around 400 pupils, in the historic Wiltshire town of Malmesbury. Our vision statement above summarises everything we aim for: a sense of community, deep learning, emotional flourishing, the excitement of discovery and setting children on a pathway to a fulfilling life.
This site is full of useful information for anyone with a child at the school, thinking of joining us or just interested in the amazing things which happen here.

pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to the website of Malmesbury Church of England Primary School. I hope you find it interesting and informative. This is a happy community, where we develop rounded children with a love of learning and the confidence to meet life's challenges. Our ethos is summed up in the statement 'Growing together in wisdom and love; discovering life in all its fullness.'
With consistently high academic results, sporting excellence and a superb building and grounds, the school has much to be proud of. However, there is never a moment for complacency, so we are constantly striving to improve. We reflect the community which we serve: one with the proudest of histories but also at the cutting edge of innovation. As a Church of England Academy our values inform, infuse and enrich everything we do. Love, Respect, Courage, Kindness, Creativity and Independence are the heart of our school.
Steve Heal, headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision & Expansion | Malmesbury C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Vision & Expansion
Our School Vision and Expansion Project
Malmesbury CE Primary School has received the support of the James Dyson Foundation to fund a £7.8 million project which will expand our school's capacity. It will also create two specialist laboratories for teaching Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts and Mathematics (STEAM subjects) where Dyson engineers will work with staff and pupils to deliver innovative learning experiences. The size of the grant and the generosity of Sir James Dyson are unprecedented in the primary school sector. In expanding, the school will gain an additional 1.6 acres of grounds. The project will be transformative, opening up a host of new opportunities for our pupils and the Malmesbury community.
Following extensive consultation with all our stakeholders, the vision presented on this page demonstrates how we plan to make the most of all the new opportunities, whilst maintaining and enhancing all that is good about our school.
Outline planning permission was granted for the project in July 2026. The school has subsequently appointed building firm Bray & Slaughter to work with us to meet all the planning conditions and to build the expansion. We anticipate that work on site will commence in March 2027. Following the completion of the build, the Gleiser Walk footpath will be continued from the West of the school site through to Poole Road, enabling easy access to the town for Backbridge residents.
Other key partners in this project are architects Wilkinson Eyre (external link, opens in a new tab) and project managers Daniel Connal Partnership (external link, opens in a new tab).

pageCache.pageTitle: Peas in the Pod | Malmesbury C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Peas in the Pod
Peas in The Pod (before & after school child care)
Peas in the Pod provides a safe, inclusive, and nurturing environment that feels distinct from the school day. The provision is designed as downtime after a busy day of learning, particularly supporting younger children who benefit from a calm, relaxed transition. It offers a space where children can unwind, socialise with friends, and feel comfortable being themselves, while continuing to develop the school's values of independence, kindness, love, respect, and courage.
Children are encouraged to enjoy a more informal atmosphere than the classroom, where play, choice, and wellbeing are prioritised. Positive relationships, mixed-age friendships, and a strong sense of belonging are at the heart of the provision.
A wide range of child-initiated and adult-led activities is available throughout each session. Children are supported to make independent choices based on their interests, helping to build confidence and self-esteem. Activities include free play, craft activities, small world play, construction, and planned adult-led activities that offer enrichment without feeling like formal learning.
There are also opportunities for children to complete homework should they wish to do so. This is optional and supported by staff where needed.
Peas in the Pod runs every day during the school term (except TD days, and for After School Club on the last day of the main terms — Christmas and Summer holidays).
£6.67 per session (includes breakfast)
£7.75 per session (includes snack)
£17.97 per session (includes snack and tea)
Arrival, Snack and Mealtimes
Children are warmly welcomed by staff on arrival and offered a snack at 3:20pm. Snacks consist of either a biscuit or two crackers, alongside a portion of fruit (a quarter or half piece, depending on the child's age). Snack time provides a gentle transition from the school day and encourages conversation, independence, and positive social interaction.
Tea is served at approximately 4:40pm and consists of two courses, freshly prepared by the school kitchen. Mealtimes are unhurried and sociable, supporting children's wellbeing, independence, and positive table manners. The termly menu is shared with families.
Outdoor Play
Outdoor play is a valued part of our provision and supports children's physical development, mental wellbeing, and social skills. Our aim is to provide access to outdoor spaces when the weather allows and when after-school clubs are not running.
Children have supervised access to the ball court, MUGA, and wild area, where they can take part in both structured and unstructured activities. These include football, den building, hide and seek, and imaginative play. Outdoor experiences promote teamwork, resilience, cooperation, and appropriate risk-taking, while allowing children to release energy in a positive way.
Screen Time and Media Use
Screen time is carefully managed to ensure it supports relaxation while maintaining a healthy balance with active, creative, and social play.
All screen use is supervised by staff, who ensure content is age-appropriate and that children are encouraged to engage in a wide range of activities throughout the session.
Registering your child for Peas in the Pod
Bookings will be made prior to the start of the academic year, for a year at a time. Any cancellations for those places will need to be made one term in advance. For example, if you wish to cancel your place in January (Term 3), you will need to notify us before the last day of term in October (Term 1). This will ensure that a place can then be offered to those on the waiting list in good time.
Places must be requested for the entire school year: September to July.
Places will be allocated as per the Peas in the Pod admissions criteria.
Once all places have been offered, a waiting list will then be held for those parents who have applied by the closing date, according to criteria.
Those parents/guardians who have applied following the deadline date will have their child's name added to the waiting list according to date of application.
If your child attends Peas and you find yourself in need of emergency childcare, you can email peasinthepod@malmesbury-pri.wilts.sch.uk or phone the school office on 01666 823514 to check Peas availability. These are called ad hoc sessions. Ad hoc sessions must not be relied upon as regular childcare as there are times we are unable to meet ad hoc requirements. Please email requests for one-off sessions, rather than asking the staff who are in ratio supervising the children.

Governors
Governing bodies are responsible for working with the school to ensure that it delivers a good quality education. Together with the Headteacher, who is responsible for day-to-day management, the governors set the school's aims and policies.
Key roles of governors: ensure clarity of vision/ethos/strategic direction; ensure accountability for educational performance and staff performance management; oversee financial performance and value for money; ensure stakeholder voices are heard; support/challenge as "critical friend".
Other duties: determining budget spend; appointing/dismissing staff; hearing appeals and grievances; setting the policies on curriculum and collective worship; setting pupil behaviour/discipline standards; ensuring buildings are welcoming and safe; setting/monitoring aims and other policies.
Further info: "Scheme of Delegation 2026-2027" (linked document).

School Tours
Deciding where to send your child to school is one of those decisions in life that you really want to get right. We are blessed with many good schools in the Malmesbury area, so we recommend that you visit a number of them. For some people a big school like ours is ideal, but others prefer the smaller schools in the surrounding villages. Finding the right school for your child is what matters, and you probably won't know until you've been inside them.
We are offering open mornings for parents/carers and children to view our wonderful school and meet some of the staff.
Each opening morning session will start at 10:00am and last approximately an hour. Please arrive at reception just before 10:00am to allow time to sign in and be given a Visitor badge.
Dates
We run open mornings for prospective parents/carers throughout the autumn term. Please contact the school office for the current list of dates and to check availability.
To book a place
Email the school office at admin@malmesbury-pri.wilts.sch.uk with: - Your name - A contact phone number for you (only used if the session has to be cancelled at short notice) - Your child's name - Your child's date of birth - The date or dates you are available to attend
You will receive an email confirmation of your booking shortly after your request is received. If the session you have requested is fully booked, you'll be offered the next available session where there is space.
Applications for a Reception year school placement starting September 2027 are currently open, with a deadline of 15th January. Applications are made via Wiltshire County Council: Apply for a school place.

Maths Mastery
The key thing about helping your child with maths is to be positive!
What is Maths Mastery @ Malmesbury?
Mastery of Maths means a deep, long-term, secure and adaptable understanding of the subject of Maths. This way of learning is something that we want pupils to acquire, so a ‘mastery Maths curriculum’ aims to help pupils, over time, acquire mastery of the subject. There are a number of elements which will help children develop mastery of Maths:
Mastery of Maths, which will build gradually as a child goes through school, is a tool for life, and immeasurably more valuable than the short-term ability to answer questions in tests or exams. We will take longer over each mathematical topic (shape, measure, addition etc.) so that early understanding is cemented deeply within each child. In order to maintain a consistent approach at school and to ensure that all objectives meet the National Curriculum we follow The White Rose Curriculum.
The National Curriculum objectives and when they are taught can be found here:
A growing confidence to reason mathematically.
Some Key features of this approach
There will be a significant amount of time devoted to developing basic number concepts. This is to build up children’s fluency as number awareness will affect their success in other areas of mathematics. Children who are successful with number are much more confident mathematicians.
Teaching for Mastery
A mastery approach to teaching and learning has been designed to support the aims and objectives of the National Curriculum.
Concrete – Pictorial – Abstract
All students, when introduced to a key new concept within Maths, will have the opportunity to build competency in this topic by taking the approach Concrete – Pictorial – Abstract, described below.
Concrete
Children will have the opportunity to use concrete objects and manipulatives to help them understand what they are doing.
Pictorial
Children will then build on this concrete approach by using pictorial representations. These representations can then be used to reason and solve problems.
Abstract
With the foundations firmly laid, children will be able to move to an abstract approach using numbers and key concepts with confidence.
Main Goal – Everyone Can Succeed
As a school we believe that all students can succeed in Mathematics. We do not believe that there are children who can do Maths and those that can’t. A positive mindset for mathematics and strong subject knowledge are key to children’s success in mathematics.
The Government published a new primary maths curriculum for Key Stages 1 and 2 in September 2013. The times tables expectations are listed below, and you can follow the link to the Gov.uk website by clicking the button to read the detailed document.
Times tables expectations
National Curriculum expectation
Count in multiples of twos, fives and tens.
Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 2, 5 and 10 multiplication tables.
Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 3, 4 and 8 multiplication tables.
Recall multiplication and division facts for multiplication tables up to 12 × 12.

Admissions
Admissions Policies
Please find on this page our current admissions policy, along with the policies for academic years 2026-27 and 2027-28.
Click on the button labelled ‘Map of Designated Areas’ to see the inner and outer designated areas, as outlined in point 6 and Appendix A of Malmesbury Primary School’s Admissions Policies. These are also downloadable via the buttons below.
The capacity of Malmesbury C of E Primary School is 420 and the Planned Admission Number (PAN) is 60.
The Governors of Malmesbury C of E Primary School have determined that the Academy will adhere to Wiltshire Council’s Schools Admissions Policy for the academic years 2026-27 and 2027-28.
Current school place spaces
We currently have spaces available in EYFS (Reception), Year 1 and Year 3. We sometimes have vacancies in other year groups too, so please call the school on 01666 823514 to enquire.
Admission to EYFS (Reception)
Wiltshire Council controls all admissions to our school. The closing date for all applications for children wishing to start in September 2026 is 15th January 2026 at noon. Notification of whether your child has a place at our school will be available to you in April 2026. For late applications (ie. after 15th January) notifications will be posted out in June 2026.
The deadline for applications for September 2027 entry will be 15th January 2027, and for September 2028 entry the deadline will be 15th January 2028.
Our staff make positive links with local pre-school groups and nurseries and arrange exchange visits where possible. An information booklet for all Reception children who start school with us in September is available by clicking on the button below.
Children must attend school full time in the term after their 5th birthday. However, most children attend school from the autumn term after their 4th birthday.
In-Year Applications
The term ‘in-year applications’ refers to all applications for places except those joining at the start of Reception year. If you are moving from another part of the country, or just want your child to change schools, this means you. The only exception would be if your child has been issued with an EHC plan for their special educational needs, in which case your Local Authority should work directly with Wiltshire Authority over your child’s school place.
Parents should apply using the in-year application form provided by the Local Authority (follow this link) and can either apply online or by paper.
Transfer to Secondary School
Transfer to Malmesbury School is made at the age of 11 years.
Strong links have been established between our school and the secondary school to ensure a smooth transition. Induction visits are arranged during Year 6, and staff from both schools maintain contact through many different links.
Admissions Policies are formally agreed and set by the Governing Body by 28 February in the determination year (the year in advance of the one in which the arrangements are to apply). The school consulted upon its admissions arrangements for the 2022/23 Admissions Policy and will consult again no later than December 2027 for the 2029/30 Admissions Policy. Following determination of arrangements, any objections to the continuation of arrangements must be made to the Schools Adjudicator no later than 15 May in the determination year.
1. I am moving to Malmesbury and want my children to come to the school. How do I apply?
All our admissions go through Wiltshire Council. If your child is already attending another school your application must be made using a School In-Year Transfer form available to download from the Wiltshire Council website.
Please be aware that the school is often over-subscribed and is usually operating a waiting list in most Year Groups.
2. What is your catchment area?
The downloadable map on this page (the ‘Map of Designated Areas’ button above) shows the Designated (catchment) Area for our school.
3. How can I find out if you have places?
Please contact the school office by e-mail at admin@malmesbury-pri.wilts.sch.uk
4. Can I put my child on your waiting list?
If you wish your child to be on the waiting list then you must make an application/in-year transfer request through Wiltshire Council stating this school as your first preference. We do not operate a separate waiting list, however you are welcome to contact the school to check the most up-to-date status of the waiting list.
5. What if I have more than one child needing a place?
You will need to apply for an In-Year Transfer for each individual child. Please be aware that we may not be able to offer places to all of your children. In such circumstances any offer of a school place will be for the child named and would not give the other children any priority for immediate admission as a sibling link. If you need places for more than one child then please contact the school for further advice.
6. Can I apply on-line?
Yes, through the Wiltshire Council website.
7. How long will it take for my application to go through?
Decision letters should be posted within 20 school days of receipt of your form although at busy periods there may be delays. For full details please see the information provided on the in-year transfer form or contact Wiltshire Council.
8. How do you choose who gets a place?
Where the school is over-subscribed places are allocated in the following priority order:
9. What happens after I am offered a place at the school?
You will have 28 days in which to accept the offer of a place and, if necessary, provide documentation to prove residency such as a valid Tenancy Agreement or evidence of exchanged contracts. You must inform Wiltshire Council if you wish to accept the place offered. They will then inform the school. Once we have confirmation of your acceptance we will contact you directly to organise start dates, class allocations etc.
10. What happens if I am not offered a place?
Wiltshire Council will make an offer of a place at whichever other of your preferred schools has availability. If you have only chosen one school or none of your preferred schools have a place then Wiltshire Council will offer you a place at your nearest available school. You will remain on our waiting list for the remainder of the academic year unless we make you an offer of a place and you decline it.
11. What if there is still no place available at the end of the academic year?
Waiting lists close at the end of the academic year (July). If you wish your child to remain on the waiting list to be considered for a place in the next academic year then you need to make a fresh application.
12. Can I appeal if I don’t get a place?
You have a right to appeal to an independent panel. If you have not been offered a place and you wish to appeal the decision then you must contact Wiltshire Council. The school must accept and cannot override the final decision of the appeal panel. You are also able to reapply in the next academic year if the appeal is unsuccessful.

School Lunches
Lunch arrangements from Sept 2026
The process of ordering school lunches is to select and pay for (if applicable) your child's meals at the time of ordering through Arbor.
Weekly menus close at 9am the Tuesday of the previous school week. Orders for the first week of every term must be placed the week before the end of the previous term (so the kitchen can purchase ingredients before the holidays). Once ordered, choices can be viewed on Arbor as a helpful reminder.
Children in EYFS, Year 1 and Year 2 get free school meals via Universal Infant Free School Meals (not charged at checkout — system aware of eligibility). Same applies for Income Based Free School Meals families, EYFS to Year 6.
It is the parent/carer's responsibility to order their child's lunch. If a child arrives without a home packed lunch and no school meal booked, it's the parents' responsibility to arrange a packed lunch to be brought in.
Link: "How to book and pay for school meals on Arbor" (help/how-to) Contact: admin@malmesbury-pri.wilts.sch.uk for further help.
Menus
The school kitchen provides a choice of hot meals and school packed lunches daily. Hot lunches are served every day on a three-week menu rotation, with different menus for Autumn, Spring and Summer terms. Main and vegetarian options, jacket potatoes with various fillings, and sandwiches with cheese, ham or tuna are offered.
If a child is absent due to illness, no charge for the booked meal. If a meal was booked but the child brings a packed lunch instead, the child eats the booked meal and takes the packed lunch home. If a child is on a class trip over lunchtime, normal meal choices don't apply — a school packed lunch can be booked separately for the trip.
Paying for lunches
Free of charge for EYFS, Year 1 and Year 2. For Years 3-6, lunches are charged at £3.00 per day, booked and paid for in advance via Arbor.
Parents experiencing payment difficulties should contact the School Office in confidence — sooner rather than later — for support options.
Years 3-6 may be eligible for free school meals depending on circumstances — link: "Free School Meals information" (Wiltshire Council website).

SCHOOL UNIFORM: - A red sweatshirt or Cardigan - A white or navy shirt or polo shirt - Navy or black trousers, shorts, skirts, or pinafores - Black shoes (No trainers) - Red gingham dresses and closed toe sandals are permitted in the summer.
Shoes
Please ensure that your children wear sensible shoes to school. Children are very active during the day both inside the school and in the playground. Their shoes need to be comfortable and safe. "Strappy" sandals are likely to cause trips and falls and boots are not allowed – in extreme weather children will be allowed to wear boots/wellingtons for their journey into school and then change into school shoes.
Hair
As shown in the adjacent picture, hair below the shoulder should be tied up so that it does not cause a hazard in P.E and sports and remains out of eyes in lessons. Hair should be natural in colour and not dyed. We do not permit tramlines and encourage blending between the longer and shorter hair.
Jewellery and Hair accessories
For safety reasons children should not wear jewellery. The only exceptions are stud earrings and essential religious items. We do not want to see children wearing hoops or dangly earrings. Please do not send your child to school with fancy headbands and clips – they are not part of school uniform. Please save these for weekends, weddings and parties!
Skirts and Shorts
Smart Watches
Children are not permitted to wear smart watches in school (watches with functionality beyond basic time-telling/date/stopwatch/alarm). Some smart watches can take photos/videos, send/receive texts, or connect to the internet — impossible to individually police which functions are active, so please keep these devices at home. Traditional analogue watches are encouraged for older children learning to tell the time.
Make Up
Make up including nail varnish is not allowed in school.

SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Information)
"The vision drives an exceptional culture of compassionate care and encouragement in which barriers to learning are overcome. This enables pupils, including those who have special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), to succeed, grow and flourish." — SIAMS report, 2026
Malmesbury Primary School prides itself on its ability to offer and successfully deliver a full and stimulating curriculum that is inclusive to all children, irrespective of need.
The SENDCo, Mrs Laura Phillips, has a great deal of experience in the role of supporting pupils with additional needs and holds the national qualification for SENCOs (NASENCO). Laura is also a Leading Inclusion Practitioner for the Local Authority, and trained to carry out SEND Reviews in schools.
Our SEND team works very closely with all of the teaching staff who, as a result, are able to support children with a wide range of academic, physical, and social needs. This may be in the form of classroom-based support or withdrawn support, sometimes in small group or one-to-one sessions, using resources from within the school and from the support services within the local authority.
The school maintains close working relationships with children, staff, parents, and other agencies. If you would like to discuss any issue regarding your child or special educational needs, please speak to our SENDCo, who will be happy to provide both information and support. Mrs Phillips is in school on Monday–Thursday.
The school is proud of its ability to support children with a variety of special needs and has taken steps to ensure that all children are treated equally. As a result, the school is suitably equipped to deal with a wide range of individual needs. The school and the governing body regularly review its provision for children with special needs and ensure that its staff are well prepared and trained.
We recognise that many special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) may not be visible and many children live with mental health challenges. For children who need additional support with these additional needs, we have two trained ELSAs (Emotional Literacy Support Assistants) who work with children on a 1:1 and small group basis across the school. In addition we have a School Counsellor who works with children individually, and a Parent Support Advisor who supports both parents and children across the school.

"The engaging, courageous and challenging curriculum is a powerful expression of the vision. This leads to pupils who are inspired to triumph in their chosen goals." — SIAMS report, 2026
Our Curriculum Intent
School vision statement: Growing together in wisdom and love; discovering life in all its fullness.
A thousand years ago, our small town was the first capital city of all England. Today, it hosts an international community of 3000 designers and engineers, at a world class research facility. Many are parents, some are governors. We soak up their expertise and spirit of innovation, combining it with the timeless beauty of the ancient and the traditional, to create the future.
Our vision is to create a learning culture that ignites young minds and gives them limitless opportunities in the twenty-first century. Today's children live in a digital age; our curriculum responds and adapts to the continuous changes in our technology-enhanced environment and society, whilst adhering to our core values of LOVE, COURAGE, RESPECT, KINDNESS, INDEPENDENCE AND CREATIVITY.
Every member of staff is engaged in dreaming, defining and delivering one key aspect of that vision: building 'Citizens of the Future.'
